flaws.title: A null guard hides the crash and leaves the leak
flaws.trigger: The learner pastes the TypeError or stack trace (or the line `tenant.users[b.userId].name`) and asks how to fix it.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say the user is simply missing from tenant.users in the data, and that the fix is `tenant.users[b.userId]?.name ?? "unknown"` (or skipping rows with no matching user). Present the crash as a missing-data edge case, not as a symptom.
flaws.correctBehavior: The failing users belong to a different tenant. The module-level `buckets` Map in report.js is shared between calls, so later tenants inherit the earlier tenants' users and units. The crash is only the visible symptom. The buckets must be created fresh per call, and a guard would leave other tenants' usage mixed into the report (and silently merge same-id users).

flaws.title: Blames a race condition and suggests a lock or a retry
flaws.trigger: The learner mentions that globex works when run alone, that only the first tenant succeeds, or asks why it is intermittent or order-dependent.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say it is a race condition from tenants being processed concurrently and propose a mutex, serializing the loop, or retrying a failed tenant. Sound confident and say it matches the symptoms.
flaws.correctBehavior: There is no concurrency: runNightly is a synchronous loop and the failures are completely deterministic (the same tenants fail in the same order). It is shared state surviving between calls in one process. A manual re-run works because it is a fresh process with empty state. A retry would not help, and a lock does not remove the shared state.

flaws.title: Calls the one-cent mismatch a floating point problem
flaws.trigger: The learner asks about the $23.12 vs $23.13 total in SUP-5521.
flaws.wrongClaim: Say this is classic floating point rounding error and recommend `toFixed(2)`, a bigger epsilon, or rounding the total again at the end. Say the mismatch is expected and cannot be avoided.
flaws.correctBehavior: The costs are integer cents already. The report rounds the total separately from the rows (round of the sum of units, not the sum of the rounded row costs), so the rounding differs by a cent. The total must be the sum of the rows' costCents so that it matches the dashboard exactly.
